definition: The claim that concepts are accessible as directions in activation space, so that separability implies a usable axis. Across 6 sources it is the assumption underneath probing and steering alike, and the archive's material is largely about where it fails to license what it is used for. Its steering form is the strong one -- if texts exhibiting a concept are linearly separable from those that do not, translating toward the positive half-space should promote the concept -- and that is exactly what the inverted-vector result falsifies, since directions with high separability can move the concept backwards. Its probing form survives better: a great deal is linearly decodable, often earlier in the network than the model's own output states it. The corpus's operative distinction is therefore that linear accessibility is well supported for reading and not for writing, and one source notes that applied work continues to build measures on outputs or embeddings even where the internal direction is available.

evidence.note: Finds directions that are highly discriminative for a concept and aligned with its positive examples yet reliably steer the model the opposite way, characterizes them geometrically as spoofing the concept's absence downstream, and turns that characterization into a training-free test that fixes the sign — improving a standard steering pipeline in 27 of 30 experiments.
evidence.title: Inverted Detection and Control in Steering Vectors

evidence.note: Compares linear probes against RFM-derived concept vectors for reading how much a sentence concerns a concept out of a frozen LLM's activations, on a human-annotated ESG benchmark, and finds the simpler probe consistently stronger.
evidence.title: Measuring Concept Content in Text from LLM Activations: ESG Evidence from Concept Vectors and Linear Probes

evidence.note: Audits four neuroscience-inspired claims about language models across 17 checkpoints from five families and 0.6B to 72B, and shows that an apparent emergence of concept steerability with scale is produced entirely by uncalibrated measurement -- raw intervention units, the readout metric, and a fixed operating point -- with correcting any one of the three removing the trend.
evidence.title: When Is a Steerable Concept Representation Real? Measurement Confounds in a Cross-Family Audit of Neuroscience Parallels in LLMs

evidence.note: Builds a Parkinson's screen from control data alone using a contrastive activation direction derived from synthetically degraded healthy speech and a nearest-neighbour anomaly score in face-encoder space, and gives a measurable precondition -- positive cosine between the synthetic and real disease directions -- that predicts in advance which modality the steering primitive will work on.
evidence.title: Label-Free Parkinson's Disease Screening from Face and Voice through Mechanistic Interpretability

evidence.note: Takes the set of active sparse-autoencoder latents as the unit of analysis and finds that adding a semantically compatible adjective to a noun deactivates 20 to 60 percent of the latents the noun alone had active, which contradicts the bag-of-features reading those sets are usually given.
evidence.title: Beyond a Bag of Features: Set-Level Instability in Sparse Autoencoders

evidence.note: Activations taken just before each explicit "Step k:" marker occupy linearly separable, step-indexed regions of representation space, and how a chain moves between those regions late in the trace predicts whether the final answer will be correct, which is used to gate interventions and to steer reasoning length.
evidence.title: LLM Reasoning as Trajectories: Step-Specific Representation Geometry and Correctness Signals

name: linear representation hypothesis
